verdict.line: You win if you close the game off your early Q-range poke before Ornn's Living Forge scaling and Brittle burst take over; you lose if the lane drags and he gets to dictate fights with his Q-E-W chain.

brief.thesis: Gnar's Q (Boomerang Throw, 1100 range) outranges both Ornn's Q (Volcanic Rupture, 800 range) and his only gap closer, E (Searing Charge, 450 range), which is why OP.GG marks this as a lane Gnar should win. But across 161 games Gnar only converts that to a 41% win rate — Ornn's passive (Living Forge) lets him forge defensive items without recalling and stack bonus armor and magic resist from everything he buys, so the early poke lead stops scaling the moment he's a couple items deep.

theirWindow.when: right after his Q lands and slows you
theirWindow.what: Volcanic Rupture slows on hit and drops a delayed magma pillar at its landing spot. If Ornn immediately dashes in with E while you're still slowed, colliding with that fresh pillar triggers a shockwave knockup around him — get your E (Hop) off the instant his Q connects or you eat the Q-E-knockup chain into a W (Bellows Breath) Brittle burst.

yourWindow.when: whenever his E is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Searing Charge (14 to 12s cooldown) is his only dash, and his Q (9 to 7s cooldown) is a slow skillshot, not a gap closer. While E is down he physically cannot reach your 1100-range Q — walk up, boomerang, and reset before he's back in range.

start.why: Picked in 63.9% of games (38.2% win rate over 131 games) because the HP and lifesteal let you sit in Q-poke range and out-sustain his Volcanic Rupture chip without needing a back.

boots.why: 50.3% pick rate; the magic resist and tenacity blunt the slow from his Q and the knockup-stun chain off his E-into-pillar collision so you aren't locked down for the follow-up Brittle burst.

core.why: The movement speed and burst-proc stacking amplify your W (Hyper) steroid, letting you stick a hit-and-run poke pattern on a melee champion with no ranged tool of his own.

runes.keystoneWhy: Higher measured win rate (47.6% vs 37.7% for the Fleet Footwork page) because the ramping attack speed stacks with your W (Hyper) proc for sustained kiting damage against a champion who can't match your range.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is run in 78.4% of games because Teleport lets you reset after shoving the wave with Q poke and E engages, banking your early gold/XP lead into tempo elsewhere since Ornn has no global pressure to punish the recall. Flash+Ignite (16.4% pick) is the alternative if you want to force the even solo-kill matchup early instead of scaling the lane.

playing.title: Poke while his E is down
playing.detail: Searing Charge is his only dash (14 to 12s cooldown); the moment it's used or whiffed, walk up and land Q (1100 range) for free since he has nothing to close the gap with.

playing.title: Dodge the Q-into-pillar-E chain
playing.detail: His Q slows and seeds a delayed magma pillar; if he dashes you with E into that pillar he gets a self-centered knockup shockwave. Use E (Hop) the instant Q lands, not after.

playing.title: Don't melee-trade while mini
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this matchup is that mini Gnar is easy to pick off all game, not just early — stay on Q poke and refuse auto-trades in his face.

playing.title: Save Rage for a real window
playing.detail: Mega Gnar's E becomes an AoE slam and unlocks R; don't transform off a random Q hit, hold the Rage bar until you can commit it into an actual all-in.

playing.title: Bait him toward walls for R
playing.detail: R (GNAR!, 90/60/30/0/0s cooldown) stuns and adds bonus damage to anyone thrown into terrain — walk the fight toward a lane wall before you use it instead of popping it in open space.

playing.title: Close the game before his items land
playing.detail: Living Forge gives him bonus armor and MR from everything he buys plus forge-anywhere item spikes, which is why a lane-advantaged matchup still sits at 41% win rate over 161 games — press the lead before level 7-9, don't let it stabilize.

playing.title: Back off after his W connects
playing.detail: Bellows Breath applies Brittle on the final gout once he's closed distance; don't keep trading autos in melee immediately after, since Brittle amplifies whatever burst follows.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, boots, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate/sample-size figures above are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical breakdown of why those numbers hold — the Q-E-pillar chain, Brittle timing, Rage management — is our own tactical read, not part of the sourced data.

stats.opponentTip: Mini Gnar’s [W] makes it easy to kill him throughout the game. Use [E] to dodge his (Q)-(E) combo or (R) to have the upper hand.
